Q: JavaScript setDate returning wrong dates A:

You are not in February - month #2 is MARCH

JS months are 0 based

 var myDate = new Date(2011, 1, 28); // 28th of Feb
 alert(myDate);
 myDate.setDate(myDate.getDate() + 1);
 alert(myDate); // 1st of March 2011 !

PS: Where you MAY have some issues are across the daylight savings time if you are creating dates using var d = new Date() and don't normalise on hours by doing d.setHours(0,0,0,0) or even d.setHours(15,0,0,0) afterwards

Q: Slashes and hashes in Perl and metacharacters A:

/ isn't special unless it's a delimiter, so it only needs to be escaped when it's used as the delimiter.

In fact, avoiding to have to escape / is a primary reason for using a delimiter other than / (i.e. to avoid "leaning toothpick syndrome").

A more detailed explanation follows.

/ is not intrinsically special in regex literals or regex patterns.

First, some terminology:

  • A regex literal is a code of the form /.../, qr/.../, s/.../.../ (or similar).
  • A regex pattern is the string actually used for matching (i.e. after interpolation has been performed).

For example, the following snippets are perfectly fine:

m{^/home/}

my $pat = "^/home/";
/$pat/

In regex literals and regex patterns, any non-word character (\W) may be escaped. But only those that would have a meaning to the literal or the regex engine must be escaped to match itself.

In a regex pattern, characters which are special in a pattern must be escaped. This may include ^, $ (as an anchor), { and \, but the specific characters set varies based on context. For example, { does not need to be escaped in a character class, ] doesn't need to be escaped outside of a character class, and spaces don't need to be escaped when the x flag isn't in effect.

Additionally, if the pattern is generated by a literal, escaping may be needed for that as well. For a regex literal (/.../, qr/.../, s/.../.../), the following must also be escaped: The delimiter, $ (as part of $name and similar) and \.

So / may always be escaped, but it only needs to be escaped when in a regex literal.

Q: python collation sort "shift-trimmed" A:

The reason your sorting isn’t matching PostgreSQL’s “shift-trimmed” behavior is that ICU (and Python’s pyicu) doesn’t fully support shift-trimmed collation.

Shift-trimmed is a very specific type of collation used in older French and some PostgreSQL setups. Its tricky part is that the quaternary weight of characters can change depending on what comes after them, and trailing weights get trimmed. That’s why a simple Collator.getSortKey won’t give the same order as your database.

A few points to keep in mind:

Using ic.Locale("und-u-ka-shifted-kb-true") gives you “shifted” collation, not shift-trimmed. Shifted moves accents after the main letters, but it doesn’t do the context-sensitive trimming that shift-trimmed requires.

ICU’s sort keys encode quaternary weights as bytes, but there’s no built-in way to apply the trailing trim logic in Python.

That’s why your attempts with c.getSortKey don’t match the AWS PostgreSQL order.

You can do this in Python

Since there’s no ready-made shift-trimmed support, you basically have three options:

Use pyuca with a modified collation table

PyUCA implements the Unicode Collation Algorithm.

You can copy the allkeys_CLDR.txt file and tweak it to simulate shift-trimmed behavior (adjust weights for trailing variables).

You can sort like this:

from pyuca import Collator
coll = Collator("modified_allkeys_CLDR.txt")
sorted_names = sorted(names, key=coll.sort_key)

This gives you programmatic control over the order, but requires manually adjusting the table.

Post-process ICU sort keys

Generate normal ICU sort keys, then write a function to trim the trailing quaternary weights according to shift-trimmed rules.

This is possible but complicated, because you have to understand ICU’s internal byte encoding.

Hard-code the order from PostgreSQL

For tests, the simplest approach may be to generate the sorted list from your database and use it as the expected order.

This isn’t dynamic, but it works if your data is mostly static and you just want reproducible tests.

Q: New TailwindCSS v4 utilities are not working in v4.1, even though the documentation lists them A:

These listed utilities all belong to block and inline type properties. They were absent in TailwindCSS for a long time, as they only appeared with the newer Baseline around 2020. Since TailwindCSS v4 targets Baseline 2023, and you can see these lists in the documentation, it's reasonable to assume they are available throughout v4. However, they were only introduced in v4.2. So you need at least v4.2 to access these new utilities.

References:

  • tailwindlabs/tailwidncss PR #19601 - Add logical block-start/block-end border, margin, and padding utilities
  • tailwindlabs/tailwidncss PR #19612 - Add logical sizing utilities (inline-size, block-size`)
  • tailwindlabs/tailwidncss PR #19613 - Add logical inset utilities (inset-s, inset-e, inset-bs, inset-be)
  • tailwindlabs/tailwidncss PR #19623 - Add font-features-* utility for font-feature-settings
  • tailwindlabs/tailwindcss.com PR #2445 - Update docs with new 4.2 utilities

Note: It's worth noting that PR #19613 also introduces a breaking change, because previously, starting from v4.0, the start-* and end-* utilities were available for the inset-inline-start and inset-inline-end properties; these have been replaced with the inset-s-* and inset-e-* utilities which is more consistent.

Q: Use Windows API Callback to retrieve Network Adapter Status A:

Just in case anyone else stumbles over this question. GetIfEntry is actually the API function for getting the operational state of a network interface. Found it by reading through the Overview of lphlpapi.h https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/iphlpapi/.

Q: ffmpeg Cannot determine format of input stream 0:0 after EOF Error marking filters as finished for some mkv video A:

the main problem is FFMPEG can't decode your MKV input for some reasons

you have 2 options here:

1 Setting analyzeduration and probesize flags

there is a good explanation somewhere in your error log

Could not find codec parameters for stream 0 (Video: h264, none(progressive), 1280x720):
unspecified pixel format Consider increasing the value for the 'analyzeduration' and 'probesize' options Input #0, matroska,webm

so setting analyzeduration and probesize flags may solve your problem:

ffmpeg -analyzeduration 2147483647 -probesize 2147483647 -i /some/path/to/video.mp4
  • 2147483647 is the max int value
  • these flags comes before the -i flag

2 Upgrade FFMPEG library version

if you are using a library, consider using the newer version which supports newer version of ffmpeg or try using another library

as you can see in this commit this problem has been solved
